title: Residue-injective finite free maps have eventually split stage lifts
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, let $(F_i,t_{ij})_{i\le j}$ be a system of finite free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with $t_{ii}=1$ and $t_{jk}t_{ij}=t_{ik}$, and let compatible maps $q_i:F_i\to N$ exhibit the $R$-module $N$ as its colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $P$ be a finite free $R$-module and $v:P\to N$ an $R$-linear map whose induced quotient map $P/\mathfrak mP\to N/\mathfrak mN$ is injective. Then there exist $i\in I$ and an $R$-linear map $v_i:P\to F_i$ such that $q_iv_i=v$ and, for every $j\ge i$, there exists an $R$-linear map $s_j:F_j\to P$ with $s_jt_{ij}v_i=1_P$. No compatibility among the $s_j$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, lemma-universally-injective-local, proof: the factorization through a finite free stage, persistence of residue injectivity, and splitting at every later stage (returned steps 4--6)

proof.text: Choose a finite basis $(e_a)_{a\in A}$ of $P$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. By clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise], choose $i_a$ and $x_a\in F_{i_a}$ with $q_{i_a}(x_a)=v(e_a)$. Starting from an arbitrary index of the nonempty $I$ and successively taking upper bounds with each $i_a$, choose $i\ge i_a$ for every $a$. Define $v_i(\sum_a r_ae_a)=\sum_a r_at_{i_ai}(x_a)$. Uniqueness of basis coordinates makes this an $R$-linear map, and the cocone identities give $q_iv_i(e_a)=v(e_a)$, hence $q_iv_i=v$. If $A$ is empty, take any $i$ and the zero map.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, lemma-universally-injective-local, proof: factorization through a finite free stage and splitting at every later stage

proof.text: Fix any $j\ge i$ and set $w_j=t_{ij}v_i:P\to F_j$. The cocone identity $q_jt_{ij}=q_i$ gives $q_jw_j=q_jt_{ij}v_i=q_iv_i=v$. Every linear map sends $\mathfrak m$ times its source into $\mathfrak m$ times its target, so this equality descends to $\bar q_j\bar w_j=\bar v$ on the quotients modulo $\mathfrak m$. If $\bar w_j(z)=0$, then $\bar v(z)=0$, hence $z=0$ by the hypothesis. Thus $\bar w_j$ is injective for this arbitrary $j$; injectivity of $\bar q_j$ is not required.

source.place: Tag 05FQ, lemma-universally-injective-local, proof: factorization through a finite free stage and splitting at every later stage

proof.text: Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], every $s\notin\mathfrak m$ is a unit. Consequently the prime residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=R_{\mathfrak m}/\mathfrak mR_{\mathfrak m}$ is $k$: the maps are $[a/s]\mapsto\bar a\bar s^{-1}$ and $\bar a\mapsto[a/1]$, whose composites are identities. Choose finite bases of $P,F_j$. For each coordinate module $R^d$, reduction identifies $R^d/\mathfrak mR^d$ with $k^d$, since its kernel is exactly the vectors with all coordinates in $\mathfrak m$. Scalar extension $k\otimes_R R^d$ identifies with $k^d$ by $c\otimes(r_a)\mapsto(c\bar r_a)_a$, with inverse $(c_a)\mapsto\sum_a c_a\otimes e_a$; the inverse identities follow by expanding $(r_a)=\sum_a r_ae_a$ and the tensor balancing relation. Both induced maps for $w_j$ are therefore its same reduced matrix. Step 2 supplies the injectivity on residue-field base change required for the finite-free residue criterion in the next step.

source.place: Tags 00E9 (lemma-characterize-local-ring) and 00O0 (lemma-cokernel-flat), finite-free residue-field calculation used in Tag 05FQ

proof.text: Apply the injective clause of [lem-pc-finite-free-map-residue-localization-strong] to the matrix of $w_j$ and the prime $\mathfrak m$. It gives $f\notin\mathfrak m$ and a left inverse $r_j$ to $(w_j)_f$. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], $f$ has an inverse in $R$. Evaluation $a/f^n\mapsto af^{-n}$ is an inverse to $R\to R_f$; on a localized module the corresponding maps are $x/f^n\mapsto f^{-n}x$ and $x\mapsto x/1$. Denote these isomorphisms by $E_P:P_f\to P$ and $E_{F_j}:(F_j)_f\to F_j$. The formula on fractions gives $E_{F_j}(w_j)_f=w_jE_P$. Hence $s_j=E_Pr_jE_{F_j}^{-1}$ is $R$-linear and $s_jw_j=E_Pr_j(w_j)_fE_P^{-1}=1_P$. The choice of $i,v_i$ was fixed in step 1 and $j\ge i$ was arbitrary, which proves every asserted clause without any compatibility claim for the $s_j$.
